extracted.intended_audience: prospective offerors/applicants to ONR BAA N00014-22-S-B001 (academia, industry, non-profits)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing and submitting full proposals (white papers, technical and cost proposals) in response to ONR BAA N00014-22-S-B001, including administrative, technical, compliance, and formatting criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and Award Recommendation Process
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR’s scientific/technical community makes the ultimate recommendation for award; recommended proposals are forwarded to ONR Contracts and Grant Awards Management for cost analysis and responsibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification that a full proposal has been recommended does not guarantee an award; Government will determine responsibility, availability of funds, and other pre-award steps. Proposals may be reviewed periodically for administrative reasons. When applicable, offerors may be required to demonstrate compliance with enhanced cybersecurity requirements prior to award (see Appendix 2, Section F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to Small Business Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR is strongly committed to providing meaningful prime and subcontracting opportunities for small businesses and socioeconomically disadvantaged categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should propose a subcontracting plan that ensures small businesses have the maximum practicable opportunity to participate consistent with efficient performance. Baseline goals should align with DoD Office of Small Business Program fiscal-year subcontracting goals; if proposed goals are below statutory requirements, include a viable written explanation and attempts taken to include small businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Plan Requirement (Contracts > $750,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed contract awards exceeding $750,000, large businesses and non-profits must provide a Subcontracting Plan that contains all elements required by FAR 19.704, FAR 52.219-9 and DFARS 252.219-7003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses are exempt. The Plan must be attached to the Proposal Checklist and will not be included in the page count. Master/Individual/Comprehensive Plans per FAR/DFARS are acceptable. Plans will be reviewed for adequacy; failure of the apparent successful offeror to negotiate an acceptable Plan within the contracting officer's time limit makes the offeror ineligible for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Resources and Posting Notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists resources to locate subcontracting partners (PTAC, DAU SB COP, Dynamic Small Business Search, SAM.gov, USAspending, Navy SBIR/STTR, etc.) and rules for transmitting notices to the Government-wide Point of Entry (SAM.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities may transmit a notice to SAM.gov to seek competition for subcontracts when (1) a contract > simplified acquisition threshold likely to result in subcontracts or (2) a subcontract opportunity > $15,000. Notices must describe the business opportunity, any prequalification requirements, and where to obtain technical data needed to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of Options
rubrics_metrics.description: Government evaluates options for award purposes by adding the total cost for all options to the total cost for the basic requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise the options during contract or grant performance. The Government reserves the right to exercise options at time of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and Evaluation Panel Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers and technical and cost proposals will be protected from unauthorized disclosure in accordance with FAR 3.104-4 and 15.207; evaluation performed by cognizant Program Officer and Government scientific experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support contractors may be used for administrative or subject-matter-expert technical consulting but selection and award decisions are solely Government personnel responsibilities. Any contractor employee with access must sign the ONR NDA for Contractor Support (includes third-party beneficiary language).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Award Notices and Pre-Award Information Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants receive notification email advising selection status; recommended applicants may be contacted for additional information required for award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional requests may include representations and certifications, revised budgets/explanations, certificate of current cost or pricing data, subcontracting plan, and other applicable information. Notification e-mail is not authorization to commit or expend funds; only an award document signed by the Contracting Officer or Grants Officer authorizes work. ONR award/modification documents available via EDA/PIEE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export Control Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors are responsible for ensuring compliance with all U.S. export control laws and regulations, including ITAR (22 CFR Parts 120-130) and EAR (15 CFR Parts 730-774), and should address whether ITAR/EAR restrictions apply to proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must obtain any required licenses or approvals (or claim exemptions) for exports of hardware, technical data, software (including deemed exports), or provision of technical assistance. Refer to ecfr.gov and export.gov resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security Classification and Classified Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Government will attempt to enable work at unclassified level; if classified material access is required, Offeror must identify need in Proposal Checklist Section II, Block 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If access to classified information is required, a DD Form 254 will be attached to the award and FAR 52.204-2 will be incorporated. ONR does not provide access to classified material under grants or cooperative agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Animals in Research
rubrics_metrics.description: If animals are to be utilized, Offeror must comply with DoD Instruction 3216.01 and DHA-MSR 6025.02 and submit Full or Abbreviated Appendix with supporting documentation (IACUC approvals, USDA Inspection Report) prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For assistance, contact ONR Animal Use Administrator. Provide required supporting documentation before award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Human Subjects in Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must protect rights/welfare of human subjects and comply with Common Rule at 32 CFR part 219 and DoD Instruction 3216.02 and other applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to award, Offerors with research involving human subjects must submit IRB approval (protocol, informed consent, documentation of IRB consideration of scientific merit, IRB registration), proof of completed human research training, Federal Wide Assurance (FWA#) and any claimed exemptions with supporting documentation and rationale signed by appropriate institutional official. Documentation submitted to ONR HRPO via Program Officer; HRPO has final judgment and approval is required before commencing work. Government will not reimburse work performed in violation. See DFARS 252.235-7004 and ONR HRPO guidance link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and Biosecurity Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must comply with DODM 6055.18 and at least the minimum applicable requirements of CDC's BMBL and NIH Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional compliance with biosafety standards; follow NIH Guidelines for rDNA and other applicable guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Involving Recombinant or Synthetic Nucleic Acid (rDNA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must not begin performance of research within scope of NIH Guidelines until ONR reviews and accepts Offeror’s documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide written statement of compliance on institutional letterhead signed by an official other than the PI; evidence of IBC approval or exemption and DHHS letter of approval or compliance. For international requirements contact ONR HRPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions and USG funding agencies subject to USG Policy for Institutional Oversight of Life Sciences Dual Use Research of Concern must comply with all listed requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposal directly involves certain biological agents or toxins, contact the cognizant Technical POC. Refer to USG S3 dual-use guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD High Performance Computing Program (HPCMP) Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees may be eligible to use DoD HPCMP assets in support of funded activities with Program Officer approval and completion of security/screening requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain ONR Program Officer approval and complete necessary security/screening. See https://www.hpc.mil/ for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project and Program Review Meetings Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR may require Project Review Meetings (typically two per year) and Program Review Meetings (generally once per year) to review progress and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume most reviews virtual in FY22 and in FY23+ approximately 40% at/near ONR Arlington VA and 60% at other facilities. Offerors may offer to host Program Review Meetings (include estimated cost and specified language in proposal); offering to host is optional and will not affect selection. Meetings will discuss only 'contracted fundamental research' and no fee charged to attendees. International ONR Global offerors should contact ONR Global Science Director for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Purchase of Foreign-Made COTS UAS Without Waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial Off The Shelf Unmanned Aircraft Systems (COTS UAS) may not be purchased pursuant to this grant/contract/prototype until a Deputy Secretary of Defense waiver is obtained, per May 23, 2018 memorandum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver not required when research is a grant, unclassified, funded with basic (6.1) or applied (6.2) research funds and performed on campus by a university. Waiver required for all other grants/assistance agreements and for all contract awards and other transaction agreements. Waiver also required for efforts interacting with military personnel, DoD property/facilities, USG labs/UARCs/FFRDCs, PAO, classified, or exploring specific military utility—these require Cyber Security waiver or ATO and Cyber Vulnerability Assessment. Prospective performers must notify Program Officer of anticipated COTS UAS purchases at white paper/proposal/award change time and provide documentation (type, effort, location). Performers must cooperate to support waiver and vulnerability assessment and may not expend federal funds or purchase until waiver and requirements met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Requirements (Grants/Contracts/TIAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting requirements differ by instrument type; see Appendix 1 for Grants/TIAs/Cooperative Agreements and Appendix 2 for Contracts and Other Transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must follow the instrument-specific reporting schedules and formats as provided in the relevant appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications Protocols and Points of Contact
rubrics_metrics.description: All UNCLASSIFIED communications must be submitted via e-mail to the Technical POC with a copy to the designated Business POC; CLASSIFIED questions handled through Security POC via an UNCLASSIFIED email request to arrange secure communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT email any classified questions. Technical questions should go to the technical area POC; business or contract questions to named contracting officer; grants questions to named grants officer; security questions to Industrial Security Specialist contact provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory File Format and Submission Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Files attached to forms must be PDF, must not contain macros, and must not be password protected. Electronic file names must not exceed 68 characters including extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an attachment is not PDF, contains macros, or is password protected, it will fail automated acceptance and be rejected. Resubmissions must be marked 'New' in SF 424 block 2 'Type of Application'. Discuss page limits for Technical Proposal with cognizant Program Officer; budgets have no page limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Proposal Formatting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical proposals must be single spaced, Times New Roman not smaller than 12 point. Discuss page limit with Program Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the technical proposal as a single PDF to R&R Other Project Information Field 8 and save the file name as 'Technical Proposal' (typing in the box prohibited). The subcontracting plan attachment is not included in page count.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424 (R&R) Form Completion and Field-Specific Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: SF-424 (R&R) must be used as the cover page; complete required fields and follow special instructions for specific fields (e.g., Field 4a: enter N00014 for new proposals; Field 4b: Agency Routing Number format with Program Office Code and Program Officer name in brackets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete SF-424 first since it auto-populates other forms. Field-specific notes include leaving Date Received by State blank; formatting for program office code (add leading zero if two digits); use Code 600 for ONRG; provide email addresses to create EDA notification profiles; indicate Minority Institution appropriately; include ONR White Paper Tracking Number in project title if applicable; ensure Authorized Representative email matches signer. Guidance links to Grants.gov forms provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project summary/abstract must identify research problem/objectives, technical approaches, anticipated outcome if successful, and impact on DoD capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only characters on a standard QWERTY keyboard, spell out Greek and non-English letters/symbols, no graphics allowed. One page or 4,000-character limit (including spaces), whichever is less. Do not include proprietary or confidential information. The abstract must be marked 'Approved for Public Release' and will be posted on the public DTIC website.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&R Other Project Information: Human Subjects, Animal Use, Environmental Compliance Fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must complete relevant R&R Other Project Information fields addressing human subject involvement (Fields 1/1a), vertebrate animal use (Fields 2/2a), and environmental compliance (Fields 4a-4d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For human subjects/animals, refer to Section F documentation requirements and submit required approvals prior to award. For environmental compliance, briefly indicate whether research will result in environmental impacts outside the laboratory and how compliance with statutes/regulations (e.g., NEPA) will be ensured. Contact Technical POC with NEPA questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Proposal Content Structure and Required Sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical proposal must include a Cover Page, Table of Contents, Technical Approach, Future Naval Relevance, Project Schedule and Milestones, Reports, Management Approach, Principal Investigator Qualifications, and Responsibility information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover Page must include 'Technical Proposal' and list (a) BAA Number, (b) Title, (c) Identity of prime offeror and list of subawards, (d) Technical contact, (e) Administrative/business contact, and (f) Proposed period of performance (base and options). Technical Approach must describe scientific/technical concepts, complete research plan, innovation, comparison to alternate approaches, and expected results. Future Naval Relevance must describe potential Naval relevance and contributions. Project Schedule/Milestones and sample reports (technical/financial progress reports, final report) should be included. Management Approach should explain rationale for key team members, relationships with subawardees/collaborators, single-PI structure if applicable. Grants do not include delivery of software/prototypes/hardware deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility Determination Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must provide information to assist ONR's evaluation of the offeror's responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe adequate resources or ability to obtain them, ability to comply with grant conditions considering existing commitments, performance history in managing Federal awards and extent previously awarded amounts will be expended prior to future awards, and record of integrity and business ethics.
